main_text.p: mulclamare[?], non posse etiam ea præ- stari, quæ imperentur. Quomodo e- nim Amynandrum Athamanum re- gem, quem in potestate non habeant, quomodo principes ejus gentis alios, quomodo Epirotas postulatos queant tradere? Simul vero contigit, ex Asia ab Antiocho Nicandrum legatum, colle- gam Thoantis opinione celerius in Æ- toliam reverti (nam duodecimo die postquam proficiscens navem consce- derat, in patriam redierat) & pecuniam cum amplis promissis adferre. Ita ex furore in novam spem sublati Ætoli ne- gocium pacis misium prorsus fecere. Quod animadvertens consul Acilius, &[illegible, ~3 letters] cognoscens, Naupactum tumultuante[illegible, ~2 letters] confluere, eamque belli sedem destin- re, quam paulo ante Menestratus Ep-[illegible, ~2 letters] rota Romanis infensus occupaverat, præmisso istuc quàm celerrimè cum ex- peditis quatuor armatorum millibus Appio Claudio, ipse mox cum toto ex- ercitu itinere difficillimo secutus Nau- pactum obsedit oppugnavitque. Et jam ferè confectam rem habebat, cum ex concilio Achæorum festinus advenit T. Quinctius Flaminius, cujus ductu Phi- lippus Macedo debellatus, & Græcia li- bertati reddita erat, cupidior servand[illegible, ~2 letters] Ætolos, quam hi merebantur. Superb enim

page.notes: Left margin: a column of dark marks and show-through from the reverse side and the edge of the neighbouring page; not transcribed. Right margin: small fragments beside lines 9, 11, 12 and 13 are too faint to read; marked as illegible. "mulclamare" (first word) is uncertain. The signature at the foot is read as "s 4" (printed as a short-s form) and is uncertain. The text is "Superb enim" with the catchword "enim" repeated; the paragraph is continuous from the previous page.
